title: market-jumpstart output (full run)
description: Structured market-research brief emitted by the market-jumpstart skill. Maps onto the markets/facts/sources tables. Per-section mode uses a smaller schema supplied by the caller ({section, facts, coverage_note, notes}); the fact definition below is the one source of truth for a fact in every mode.

market.description: The shared vocabulary every section (and every downstream slide) must reuse verbatim. Produced by the scout; echoed back unchanged on a full run.

includes.description: One sentence: what this market covers.

excludes.description: One sentence: what is deliberately out of scope.

categories.description: Exactly 3 segment names, reused verbatim by every section and every slide that names a segment.

customer_org_type.description: Buying organization type. Must read naturally after both 'Key players in ___ have' and 'Within ___,' — use an article or a plural, never a bare singular.

coverage_outlook.description: How much free public coverage this sub-market has. Be pessimistic: 'thin' when only the parent market is broken out by free sources.

coverage_note.description: Rendered to the human. What free sources could not supply for this market, stated plainly. Null when coverage was fine. Never an excuse for an invented number — it exists so the number can be absent.

text.description: The fact as a human reads it, with its attribution inline ('… per Grand View Research, 2025'). Prefixed '(dated) ' when stats.year is more than 3 years old. Prefixed 'SUGGESTED CATEGORY: ' on a definition fact proposing an assessment category this section list does not cover.

fact_date.description: Publication date of the primary source — NOT the year the figure refers to (that is stats.year). Month-only or year-only sources use the first day and say '(date approximate)' in the text.

group_key.description: Shared across facts describing the same underlying item — AND across conflicting estimates of the same quantity (e.g. two TAM figures for US 2024 both get 'tam-us-2024'). Conflicting estimates are kept as separate facts and rendered side by side; they are never merged, averaged, or dropped.

importance.description: 9-10 TAM or CAGR from a named research firm / a rule that reshapes the market / a published top-vendor share; 6-8 major acquisition or funding round / published segmentation split / adoption survey / named leader with evidence; 4-5 sourced challenge or pain point / pricing model / persona title / category example; 1-3 color, vendor marketing claim, minor deal.

stats.description: Structured values a source actually states; null when the fact type has no stat shape. Set stats.type to name the shape. Shapes — tam: {type,value,unit,year,geography,segment,basis,is_forecast}; cagr: {type,rate_pct,window_start,window_end,geography,segment,is_forecast}; share: {type,player,share_pct,year,basis}; concentration: {type,top_n,share_pct,year}; segment_split: {type,dimension,year,segments:[{label,share_pct}]}; acquisition: {type,acquirer,target,deal_value,announced}; funding: {type,company,amount,round,lead_investors[]}; adoption: {type,metric,value_pct,population,year}; pricing: {type,model,basis,typical_range}; player: {type,name,domain,tier,category,why}; persona_item: {type,persona:'purchaser'|'user'|'shared',kind:'title'|'pain'|'want',value}; process_item: {type,process,kind:'cost'|'motivation'|'pain',value}; regulation: {type,rule,authority,status:'in_force'|'pending'|'proposed',effective_date,changes}. Only include keys a source states outright — never derive, annualize, convert, sum, or interpolate a value.
